title: Platform systems & services: integrated playbook (how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical platform systems & services playbook for the Platform team. It aggregates how-tos, dashboards and alerting guidance, operational runbooks, retrospective summaries, and the near-term roadmap. The goal is to provide a single reference for on-call engineers, product-facing Platform owners, and cross-functional partners (SRE, infra, serving-runtime).

Scope

- Systems covered: control-plane (platform-control-plane), tenant-router, kube-orchestration, metrics-collector, secrets-manager, storage-proxy.
- Topics: production how-tos, dashboards and alert definitions, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective outcomes and action items, roadmap priorities, and team wiki organization.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner_team: engineering (Platform).
- On-call rotation: Platform Oncall (pager duty schedule: platform-oncall).
- Secondary owners: eng-sre (for infra-level failures), eng-serving-runtime (for downstream inference regressions).
- Escalation path: on-call -> platform oncall lead -> eng-sre -> engineering director. Use PagerDuty escalation policies defined in /ops/pd/policies.

SLAs and SLOs

- Control plane API availability: SLO = 99.95% monthly. Error budget tracking in the Platform dashboard.
- Request router latency (p95): SLO = 50ms.
- Job scheduling latency (99th percentile): SLO = 2s.
- Critical alerting target: pages for severity=P1 within 5 mins on-call acknowledgement.

Systems & services inventory (short)

- platform-control-plane (owner: Platform Core) - REST API for tenant and route management. Depends: auth, db-cluster.
- tenant-router (owner: Routing) - routes customer inference traffic to appropriate pools. Depends: service-discovery, egress-proxy.
- metrics-collector (owner: Observability) - scrapes and forwards metrics/traces to central systems.
- secrets-manager (owner: Security) - integrates with KMS/HSM for key retrieval.

How-tos (common operational tasks)

1) Deploy a control-plane patch (canary -> prod)
   - Preconditions: CI green, performance tests passed, no active P1 incidents.
   - Steps:
     1. Open PR and add canary label per release checklist.
     2. Trigger canary deploy using /deploy/canary.sh --service platform-control-plane --version vX.Y.Z.
     3. Monitor canary dashboard (link below) for 15m: error rate, latency, CPU/mem.
     4. If stable, promote with /deploy/promote.sh --service platform-control-plane --to prod.
     5. Post-deploy: run smoke tests (/scripts/smoke-platform.sh) and update release notes.
   - Rollback: /deploy/rollback.sh --service platform-control-plane --to <last-stable>.

2) Add an alert to the routing dashboard
   - Open the Grafana folder: grafana/dashboards/routing.json in repo.
   - Create a new alert rule with: condition = WHEN (sum(rate(router_errors_total[1m])) by (instance) > 5) FOR 2m.
   - Ensure annotation includes runbook link and owner tag: @owner:Routing.
   - Test alert using --dry-run then commit to repo and create a PR.

3) Onboarding a new Platform engineer (wiki setup)
   - Task list: RBAC access, PagerDuty, Slack channels (#platform-ops), Confluence permissions, dev cluster credentials.
   - Provide new hire with checklist: /onboarding/platform-onboarding.md and assign buddy.

Dashboards & alerts

- Primary dashboards (Grafana):
  - Platform Overview: grafana/internal/dashboards/platform-overview (SLOs, global health, top-5 alerts).
  - Control Plane Canary: grafana/internal/dashboards/control-plane-canary (canary error rates, p95 latencies, CPU/mem).
  - Routing Health: grafana/internal/dashboards/routing-health (inflight requests, error heatmap, backend capacity).
  - Job Scheduler: grafana/internal/dashboards/job-scheduler (queue depth, scheduling latency).
  - Observability Pipeline: grafana/internal/dashboards/observability-pipeline (ingest rates, tail drop, downstream latency).

- Alerting guidance (severity assignment and thresholds):
  - P1 (page): service-down, total-error-rate > 5% sustained for 2m, control-plane unavailable, metrics ingestion stopped for > 5m.
  - P2 (slack alert): high error spike (between 2% and 5%), queue depth > threshold for 10m, elevated 95th latency beyond SLO by 2x for 5m.
  - P3 (email/ticket): non-urgent configuration drift, increases in non-critical errors.

Example alert table (for quick copy/paste)

| Alert name | Condition | Severity | Owner | Runbook |
|------------|-----------|----------|-------|---------|
| ControlPlane_API_ErrorRate | sum(rate(control_plane_errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(control_plane_requests_total[1m])) > 0.05 for 2m | P1 | Platform Core | platform-control-plane-runbook |
| Router_Backend_Overloaded | router_backend_inflight_requests > 1000 for 5m | P2 | Routing | routing-scaling-runbook |
| Metrics_Forwarder_Delay | histo_quantile(0.95, latency_seconds_bucket) > 30s for 10m | P1 | Observability | observability-pipeline-runbook |

Runbooks (operational playbooks)

- platform-control-plane-runbook (summary)
  - Trigger conditions: high 5xx rate, database connectivity errors, auth failures.
  - Immediate steps (0-5m):
    1. Acknowledge page in PagerDuty.
    2. Check platform-control-plane canary dashboard for error spikes and trace links.
    3. Check DB connectivity: kubectl exec -n platform platform-control-plane -- /bin/check-db.sh.
    4. If DB is unhealthy, open incident with eng-sre and follow DB incident runbook.
  - Mitigation (5-30m):
    1. If error due to recent deploy, roll back using deploy/rollback.sh.
    2. If rate spike from client, enable temporary rate-limiter: /admin/rate-limit --tenant <id> --limit 10rps.
  - Recovery (30m+):
    1. Verify SLOs restored and run postmortem template.
    2. Communicate status in #platform-status and update incident tracker.

- routing-scaling-runbook (summary)
  - Trigger conditions: high backend latency, inflight requests > 90% of capacity, repeated 503s.
  - Steps:
    1. Confirm backend node health in cluster autoscaler console.
    2. Temporarily route traffic to standby pool: /routing/switch-pool --from pool-a --to pool-b --drain 300s.
    3. Scale up routing pool: kubectl scale deployment routing --replicas=<n>.
    4. If GPU-backed pools are saturated, trigger capacity request to capacity slack channel and notify Sales for affected customers.

Post-incident retrospectives

- Format: timeline (what happened), impact (who/what was affected), root cause, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates.
- Recent summary (Jan 2026):
  - Incident: Observability pipeline partial outage (2026-01-08) caused delayed alerting for 25m.
  - Root cause: misconfigured retention policy on an intermediate Kafka topic leading to consumer lag.
  - Actions taken: automated retention config test added to deployment CI, failover consumer group created, dashboard now shows consumer lag more prominently.
  - Open action items: (1) CI test owner: Emilia Zhang, due 2026-02-01 (DONE). (2) Add synthetic alerting from an independent probe: Daniel Kim, due 2026-03-01 (IN PROGRESS).

Roadmap (next 6 quarters high-level)

- 2026 Q2:
  - Complete unified platform overview dashboard with SLO burn-down.
  - Introduce automated canary rollback on defined regressions.
  - Improve tenant self-service tooling for routing policies.
- 2026 Q3:
  - Pilot private deployment observability connectors for on-prem customers.
  - Implement cost-aware routing knobs in tenant-router.
- 2026 Q4:
  - Multi-region control-plane failover improvements and DR runbook.
- 2027 Q1:
  - RBAC hardening and audit logging improvements.
  - Dashboarding expansion for model-serving telemetry (KV cache hit rates, batching efficiency).

Team wiki & knowledge organization

- Recommended structure (top-level pages):
  - Platform playbook (this page)
  - Systems & services (per-service pages with ownership, dependencies, SLOs)
  - Dashboards & Alerts (dashboard links, alerting policy, template alert rules)
  - Runbooks (searchable by alert name and service)
  - Retrospectives (sorted by quarter)
  - Onboarding & run rate docs (checklists and access requests)

- Tagging convention: use labels like "service:<service-name>", "slo:<name>", "runbook", "dashboard" to make pages discoverable. Keep page titles short and kebab-case for file export compatibility.

Operational conventions and best practices

- All alert rules must include a runbook link and an owner annotation.
- No silent auto-restarts: if a restart resolves an incident, capture root cause in the postmortem — restarts are mitigation, not resolution.
- Release cadence: minor patch releases weekly, major releases quarterly. Use canaries for all production changes.
- CI gates: integration tests, perf smoke, and observability self-checks must pass before prod promotion.

Appendices & useful commands

- Useful kubectl snippets:
  - View platform-control-plane pods: kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=platform-control-plane
  - Tail logs: kubectl logs -n platform <pod> -c app --follow

- Common scripts:
  - /deploy/canary.sh --service <name> --version <v>
  - /deploy/promote.sh --service <name> --to prod
  - /admin/rate-limit --tenant <id> --limit <rps>

- Links (internal)
  - Grafana root: grafana/internal
  - PagerDuty: https://pd.internal/policies/platform
  - Incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/team/platform
  - CI pipelines: https://ci.internal/pipelines/platform
